name: Mercury
description: The smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest to the Sun.
about: Mercury completes an orbit around the Sun in just 88 days, but it spins so slowly on its axis that a single solar day there lasts about 176 Earth days. With no atmosphere to trap heat, its cratered surface swings from over 400 °C during the day to nearly -180 °C at night.

name: Venus
description: The hottest planet in the Solar System, wrapped in clouds of sulfuric acid.
about: Venus is similar in size to Earth, but its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere creates an extreme greenhouse effect that keeps the surface above 460 °C. It spins in the opposite direction to most planets, and its day is longer than its year.

name: Earth
description: Our home, the only planet known to harbor life.
about: Earth is the largest of the rocky planets and the only one with stable liquid water on its surface. Its nitrogen- and oxygen-rich atmosphere and its magnetic field shield life from solar radiation, while the Moon stabilizes the tilt of its axis and helps keep the climate relatively steady.

name: Mars
description: The Red Planet, home to the largest volcano in the Solar System.
about: Mars gets its reddish color from the iron oxide covering its surface. The planet is home to Olympus Mons, a volcano about 22 km tall, and Valles Marineris, a canyon system more than 4,000 km long. There is evidence that liquid water was once abundant there, making Mars one of the main targets in the search for past life.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet in the Solar System, with a storm bigger than Earth.
about: Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm that has been observed for over 350 years, and the planet is surrounded by dozens of moons, including Ganymede, the largest moon in the Solar System, and Europa, which hides an ocean beneath its icy crust.

name: Saturn
description: The lord of the rings, famous for its dazzling system of icy rings.
about: Saturn's rings are made of billions of chunks of ice and rock and stretch for hundreds of thousands of kilometers. The planet is so low in density that it would float in water, and its moon Titan is the only one in the Solar System with a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane.

name: Uranus
description: The blue-green giant that spins on its side.
about: Uranus has its rotation axis tilted by about 98 degrees, so it practically rolls around the Sun. Because of this, each pole spends 42 years in continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness. Its color comes from methane in the atmosphere, which absorbs red light.

name: Neptune
description: The farthest planet from the Sun, with the fastest winds in the Solar System.
about: Neptune was the first planet discovered through mathematical calculations before it was ever observed. Its winds reach over 2,000 km/h, and its largest moon, Triton, orbits in the opposite direction to the planet's rotation, suggesting it was captured from the Kuiper Belt.

name: Pluto
description: The most famous dwarf planet, with a heart of nitrogen ice.
about: Pluto was considered the ninth planet until 2006, when it was reclassified as a dwarf planet. In 2015, the New Horizons probe revealed mountains of water ice, heart-shaped plains of frozen nitrogen and a thin bluish atmosphere. Its largest moon, Charon, is nearly half its size.
